output.brief: The rejections trace to our own paperwork, not the fungicide, Lower Serra fruit or Meridane's equipment. When Meridane bookings moved to the new Tallis system, the mandarin product record was copied from the avocado record, so every Meridane mandarin container was sent at 7.0°C instead of our 4.0°C specification. The carrier's controller downloads show units ran to 7.0°C within 0.4°C. All five containers at 7.0°C were rejected, with decay of 9–14%. All four at 4.0°C passed, whether they went by Coastway or Meridane, and whether the fruit was packed with old or new fungicide. I'm about 90% sure. Lower Serra pallets were somewhat worse inside the failed containers, but they made up only 28–40% of each load, and no accepted containers were surveyed. That is a secondary effect that is not established as a cause. Next steps: first, correct the temperature in PRD-MAND-01 and have Meridane reset the container at sea and the one queued for 10 Oct. Second, add a check that compares container settings with the product specification before submission. Don't suspend Lower Serra, don't claim refrigeration failure against Meridane, and don't switch fungicide on this evidence. Review how the product master was signed off before deciding any contractor charge-back.
